title: Delegated Access, Change-Gates, and Travel Claims Playbook
author: Miguel Torres
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the combined end-to-end processes for delegated access requests, change-management gates when requests affect permissions or spend, and the procedure for travel claim submission and adjudication. It is intended to reduce approval latency, maintain strong auditability, and ensure consistent financial controls across regions.

Audience and scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved vendors.
- Covers role-based access requests, temporary and emergency exceptions, vendor service account provisioning, change reviews with cost impact, and corporate travel & expense claims.

Principles:
- Least privilege: default deny and time-bound privileges.
- Traceable delegation: all approver delegations must be recorded and rotated annually.
- Cost-aware changes: Finance reviews any change that increases monthly committed spend by >=10%.
- Consistent receipts: receipts required for line items > $25 USD; exceptions require manager attestation.

Quick glossary:
- Request Center: internal portal for submitting access, vendor, and expense requests.
- Delegation Registry: canonical list of approver delegations and expiry dates.
- CAB: Change Advisory Board for cross-domain or high-risk changes.

Access request categories and SLAs:
1) Tier A  (Non-sensitive, read-only data): Manager approval -> Automated provisioning. SLA: 48 business hours.
2) Tier B (Production deploy, write, or infra access): Manager + Security review -> Provisioning with audit log. SLA: 5 business days.
3) Tier C (Privileged admin, KMS or crypto operations): Manager + Security + Head of Service -> Multi-factor enrollment and just-in-time (JIT) where possible. SLA: 10 business days.
4) Emergency access for incident response: On-call manager approve -> Security on-call notified -> Grant with strict 8-hour expiry -> Post-incident review within 72 hours.

Delegation and rotation rules:
- Approver delegation may be granted to an explicit alternate (name and email) for up to 12 months. Delegations must be recorded in the Delegation Registry and include a rotation date.
- Delegations older than 12 months automatically expire and generate a renewal reminder to the owner.
- Delegated approvals inherit the same risk posture as primary approver and must complete any required training (security, procurement, or travel policy) prior to approval.

Exception lifecycle:
- Create an Exception Record via the Request Center with: justification, risk assessment summary, compensating controls, owner, expiry date, and link to affected assets.
- Security classifies the exception as low/medium/high risk. High-risk exceptions require weekly review and a mitigation plan.
- Renewal requires original approver chain sign-off. Exceptions longer than 90 days escalate to the Risk Committee.

Change-management gates when requests affect permissions or spend:
- Any request that touches IAM, network ACLs, KMS, or billing/configurable infra must include a Change Statement: scope, rollback plan, expected cost delta, and test/runbook references.
- Automated triage flags changes where estimated monthly spend delta >=10% for Finance review and where more than two services are touched for CAB scheduling.
- CAB review is required for policy-level changes (default session duration, cross-region access policies) and multi-team rollouts.

Vendor onboarding tied to access provisioning:
Required attachments for vendor requests that will receive service accounts: signed contract or SOW, vendor security attestation (SOC2 or equivalent), IP allowlist (if relevant), and a named vendor owner within Redwood. Finance must approve when expected vendor spend > $5,000/month. Default vendor service accounts are created with minimal privileges and require an owner to rotate credentials quarterly.

Travel & expense process (summary):
- Pre-trip approval: International trips require manager pre-approval; estimated total > $7,000 require VP sign-off.
- Allowed classes: Economy preferred; premium/elevated travel allowed only with prior approval for trips >6 hours flight time or Executive-level roles.
- Meals and per-diems: Region-specific caps published monthly in the policy portal. Attach receipts for any single item > $25 USD.
- Lost receipts: submit the Receipt Exception Form with manager attestation; Finance may approve up to $75 per item without a receipt when pre-authorized.
- Submission window: expenses must be filed within 30 days of trip end; late submissions require manager+finance sign-off.

Expense approval tiers:
- Tier 1: < $500 — Manager approval.
- Tier 2: $500$5,000 — Manager + Finance reviewer.
- Tier 3: > $5,000 — Manager + Finance + Director.

Retention and audit evidence:
- Access request records, approvals, and audit logs: retain 7 years.
- Exception records: retain 7 years for regulated accounts; otherwise retain 3 years.
- Vendor onboarding artifacts and contracts: retain 10 years post-termination.
- Travel receipts and T&E records: retain 6 years to satisfy cross-jurisdictional tax requirements.

Operational runbook (step-by-step):
1) Submit the request in Request Center using the appropriate form (Access Request / Vendor Onboard / Travel & Expense). Include justification, estimated cost, assets impacted, and requested expiry.
2) Auto-triage: system assigns reviewers based on request type and flags CAB/Finance/Security as needed.
3) Approver notifications: approvers receive an in-portal task and an email. Approvers are expected to action within the SLA or reassign via the Delegation Registry.
4) Fulfillment: engineering or IAM tooling performs provisioning and records the request_id in audit-index.
5) Close and tag: the Request Center applies retention tags and closes the request. Any deviations should create a post-fulfillment incident for follow-up.

Common scenarios (short guidance):
- Incident remediation: use the Emergency Exception path, include incident ID, and do the post-incident privilege review.
- Vendor needs a service account: attach vendor checklist and security attestation; limit privileges and set credential rotation.
- International travel with missing receipt: attach Receipt Exception Form and manager attestation; expect Finance review.

Controls and metrics (governance):
- SLA targets: Tier A 90% within 48 business hours; Tier B 95% within 5 business days.
- Exception maturity: 95% of exceptions reviewed before expiry.
- Financial gate effectiveness: 100% of changes with estimated spend delta >=10% routed to Finance for review.

Contacts and escalation points:

- Security exceptions: sec-exceptions@redwood.ai

Review cadence and ownership:
- Annual policy owner: Finance-Legal (policy review each January).
- Quarterly risk & exception review: Security + Compliance.
- Delegation registry audit: People Ops + Security annually.
